catalog_quote: These two languages are closely similar in their pronominal systems. The two make use of both independent and dependent pronouns, also sometimes referred to as free and bound. The former, like full noun phrases, carry stress or accent, and they can be uttered in isolation or in any ‘argument position’ (e.g. subject, object, indirect object), like any full noun phrase. The latter, however, are unstressed (atonic) and phonologically dependent—they must, so to speak, ‘lean’ on some other word. ... Some of the Wik languages, including Wik-Me’nh, Wik-Mungkan, Wik-Ngathan, and Wik-Ngatharr, have undergone an important sound change that has resulted in the reduction of unstressed post-consonantal vowels—i.e. unstressed vowels in the V-position of CV syllables.
